task.name: An unversioned alias is the routing candidate, so evidence accrues to a moving target and earlier versions cannot be offered as alternatives
task.story_text:
## Why

A routing candidate is currently allowed to be a model family rather than a model. Some catalog
entries name an unversioned vendor alias, which the vendor resolves at invocation time to whichever
concrete version it currently ships. The candidate the router reasons about, the identity recorded
against the run, and the accumulated evidence are all keyed to the alias, not to what actually ran.

This has two consequences, and the second is easy to miss.

**Evidence accrues to a moving target.** Observations gathered under an alias describe whatever the
alias meant at the time. When the vendor advances it, the history continues accumulating under the
same key as though the subject were unchanged. A consumer applying a sample floor, a recency
weighting, or a cost cohort to that history is treating observations of two different models as
observations of one, and nothing marks the discontinuity.

**Earlier versions cannot be offered as alternatives.** An alias can only mean the current release,
so a previous generation is not expressible as a candidate at all — even when it is cheaper, and
even when it is sufficient for the work being routed. This is not hypothetical: a single provider
currently serves more than forty models spanning several generations at materially different price
points, and the catalog can name only the newest of each family. A router whose purpose is choosing
among candidates on evidence cannot choose a candidate it has no way to name, so the entire
cost-versus-capability tradeoff across generations is unavailable by construction.

Aliases are still worth having. Tracking a family's current release is a reasonable default and is
why one provider's entries stayed current here while another's fell two generations behind. The
defect is that an alias is currently the *only* thing expressible for those families, and that what
it resolved to is neither recorded nor available to reason about.

## Acceptance criteria

- A specific model version is expressible as a routing candidate for any provider that publishes
  versions, alongside — not instead of — the family alias.
- Where a candidate names a family rather than a version, the version that served is recorded
  against the run and is distinguishable from the family name that selected it.
- Evidence accumulated for a family alias is attributable to the versions that produced it, so a
  consumer can tell whether a population describes one model or several.
- A change in what an alias resolves to is detectable from recorded runs rather than only from a
  behavioural surprise.
- Nothing requires an operator to pin a version: a configuration naming only aliases keeps working
  and keeps tracking current releases.

## Example

What the catalog can express today versus what the provider actually serves:

```
catalog can name        opus                    (whatever ships today)
                        sonnet                  (whatever ships today)

provider serves         claude-opus-5           $5 / $25
                        claude-opus-4-8         $5 / $25
                        claude-haiku-4-5        $1 / $5
                        ...and further versions per family

recorded against runs   anthropic/opus/cli      the alias — the version is not the identity
```

A run that used the alias records the alias. If the alias advances a generation, the next run
records the same identity for a different model, and the two are indistinguishable in the history
that routing consumes.

Depends on #2252

handoff.summary: Made a concrete model version a first-class routing candidate alongside the family alias, and made what an alias actually served a recorded, queryable, attributable fact. Catalog (config/data/models.yaml) gains pinned Anthropic CLI entries — claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-4-6, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5 — beside the opus/sonnet/haiku shorthands as separate registry identities, so an alias-only configuration is unaffected while an earlier generation becomes nameable. model_profiles.canonical_id_for_legacy_key no longer folds a concrete version onto its family shorthand (the #2225 prefix heuristic is removed); a version resolves to its own entry or stays visibly unresolved. audit_substrate gains a role-neutral invocation_identities table (SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION 7->8) indexing configured and resolved identity per recorded invocation, drawn from both cost.agents and the superseded preflight.attempts ledgers, derived from raw_json on open so it covers already-indexed history; alias_resolution_timeline() plus a new `forge audits alias-drift` subcommand make an alias-resolution change detectable from records. On the evidence side RunOutcome / RoleAttempt / ReviewerAttempt / ReviewerValueSample carry the served identity, every role bucket gains a by_resolved_model breakdown, and get_dev_signal / get_dev_domain_signal / get_role_reliability_signal / get_review_signal / get_reviewer_value_signal all report a resolved_population (by_resolved_model / distinct / mixed / attributed / unattributed). An alias-served run is additionally projected onto the served version's own profile entry in a separate alias_derived section carrying by_configured_model, so a pinned candidate is rankable from alias history while per-candidate counts stay authoritative and no cross-candidate aggregation sees the run twice.

story_deviations: Pinned claude-opus-5 and claude-sonnet-5 with cost_rank_basis: vendor-tier and NO cost block rather than inventing per-MTok figures. Both are the currently-served versions in this repo's audit history but neither has an attributable price in PRICING_TABLE or the story. Declaring a literal I cannot vouch for is the exact defect config/pricing.py exists to prevent; a vendor-tier band is the same trust posture the shorthands already carry. Adding real figures later upgrades them to price-attributed entries with no code change.

Did not pin claude-opus-4-8 (27 occurrences in recorded audits) for the same reason — no attributable price. claude-opus-4-6 is already an earlier generation with a real price, so the 'earlier version is expressible' criterion is satisfied without it. It is used in the test suite as the worked example of a project-declared pin.

Added ('anthropic', 'claude-haiku-4-5'): (1.00, 5.00) to runners/schema_utils.PRICING_TABLE. Sourced from the story's own Example block and consistent with the haiku shorthand's existing literal; without it the pinned entry would route fine and then record cost-unknown.
deferred_items: Server-dated spellings such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (213 occurrences) and claude-opus-4-8 (27) now record as resolution=unresolved instead of folding into the family shorthand. This is the intended contract — the fold was the defect — and alias-drift surfaces it, but those runs lose canonical grouping until a catalog entry pins them. A one-line models.yaml entry each closes it; not done here because neither has an attributable price.

The alias_derived projection on a concrete candidate is reported but not yet consumed by ranking: assignment.py still ranks a pinned candidate on its own direct evidence only. Folding alias-derived evidence into a rate is a routing-behaviour change beyond this story's ACs and should be decided deliberately (it is weaker evidence — gathered while something else was selected — which is why by_configured_model marks its provenance).

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the review findings without changing the approach. P1: the resolved_population attribution double-counted non-dev evidence. The preflight, planner and review profile sections each carry two populations folded from one run at different call sites — 'runs' (phase cost/cycles) and '_attempted_count' (per-invocation completion) — and iteration 0 wrote both into a single by_resolved_model breakdown, so a run carrying both phase-level and attempt-level telemetry reported two attributed observations of the served version while the signal divided its rate by one attempt. Each breakdown is now scoped to the counter it explains: RESOLVED_MODEL_BREAKDOWN_KEY ('by_resolved_model') sums to 'runs' and is written by the dev buckets and the phase-level folds (_update_review, _update_preflight, _update_planner); RESOLVED_MODEL_ATTEMPT_BREAKDOWN_KEY ('by_resolved_model_attempts') sums to '_attempted_count' and is written by the completion folds (_update_review_completion, _update_role_completion). _resolved_population gained a matched (key, total_key) pair, and get_review_signal / get_role_reliability_signal now read the attempt-scoped breakdown against their own '_attempted_count' denominator while get_dev_signal / get_dev_domain_signal / get_reviewer_value_signal keep reading the runs-scoped one. _fold_resolved_model also gained a 'count' parameter so the review section's cycles-weighted 'runs' gets a cycles-weighted breakdown rather than a per-call tally that could never reconcile with it — the same class of defect one level down. P2 (adjacent to the changed code, fixed per the in_scope policy): alias_resolution_timeline reported a stale 'current' for an A -> B -> A timeline because resolved_models is ordered by first appearance and 'current' read its tail; the newest resolution is now tracked while iterating (rows arrive oldest-first) and reported directly, leaving the first-appearance ordering intact for the history itself. No production behaviour from iteration 0 was otherwise altered: rates, sample floors, weighting, the catalog, the substrate schema and the alias_derived projection are unchanged.

findings.description: When preflight, planner, or review telemetry records both phase-level data and attempt-level data for the same invocation, the routing signal's resolved_population reports more attributed version runs than the signal's actual population contains.
When an alias resolves to version A, then version B, then version A again, alias_resolution_timeline reports current as version B even though the newest recorded invocation resolved to version A.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 changes canonical_id_for_legacy_key semantics but does not list src/theforge/cli/profiles.py:134, which calls it in the profiles-migration display path, nor model_profiles.py:2833/2910 migration callsites beyond the named tests. The signature is unchanged so nothing breaks at import, but a key that previously folded to anthropic/sonnet/cli and now resolves to a pinned id (or stays unresolved) will change what forge profiles migration reports.
  Suggestion: While implementing Step 2, check the three existing callsites and confirm the migration/report path treats a newly-pinned canonical id and a still-unresolved key correctly rather than as an ambiguity regression.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 does not state how the new pinned Anthropic entries satisfy the catalog's attribution rules — cost_rank_basis must be stated whenever the band is not the entry's own attributable price band, and an unstated, underivable band is a load error (models.yaml header, config/pricing.py, model_duplicates._ROUTING_READS).
  Suggestion: Pin the concrete entries with pricing_provenance naming the billed identity (PRICING_TABLE already carries claude-opus-4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6) so their bands derive from their own attributable prices; only fall back to cost_rank_basis where a price cannot be attributed.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 folds the same admissible run into both the configured alias bucket and the resolved concrete model's profile entry. Aggregate counts across candidates (sample floors applied fleet-wide, cost cohorts, any 'total observations' read) can now see one run twice.
  Suggestion: Keep per-candidate counts authoritative and mark alias-derived evidence on the concrete entry so any cross-candidate aggregation can exclude the duplicate projection.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 bumps SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION (currently 7, the DB-schema counter) while a separate per-record migration chain exists up to _migrate_v9_to_v10 in the same module. The plan does not say which counter it means.
  Suggestion: Confirm the new table is a DB-schema change only (SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION + _MIGRATIONS list + a reindex helper modeled on _reindex_dev_model_identity) and that no record-level MIGRATION_HELPERS entry is implied.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Preflight named src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py and model_identity.py as likely files; Step 1 lists config/models.py instead. This is probably correct (the catalog is data-driven and models.py owns AGENT_REGISTRY/known_raw_model_key_prefixes), but the parser may still need to accept a pinned entry beside an alias of the same family.
  Suggestion: If load_packaged_catalog or the duplicate/identity checks reject two same-provider entries in the same family, extend model_catalog.py rather than working around it in the data file.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 3 says the new role-neutral invocation index will be populated from cost.agents, but not every recorded invocation lives there today: earlier preflight retry/fallback attempts are recorded only under preflight.attempts[*].ledger (src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py, src/theforge/coordinator/audit_render.py). If the intended contract is truly 'every recorded invocation', limiting the index to cost.agents would miss that path.
  Suggestion: Either include preflight.attempts[*].ledger in the new index, or narrow the step/CLI contract to top-level cost.agents invocations so the implementation and operator surface stay truthful.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Steps 4-5 describe version-aware profile evidence, but assignment.py routes from .forge/model_profiles.yaml, and the current update path (src/theforge/model_profiles.py:update_from_run) only appends new runs. There is no existing rebuild-from-audit path for historical profile aggregates, so previously mixed alias history would stay opaque unless the implementation adds one.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit migration/backfill decision in src/theforge/model_profiles.py (and, if needed, src/theforge/cli/migrate_profiles.py): either rebuild/populate the new resolved-version breakdown from recorded audit ledgers, or surface legacy pre-breakdown populations as explicitly unknown/mixed until fresh runs refill them.
- [P2] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 4 relies on resolved identity reaching all reviewer-value evidence, but the native plan-review value capture currently writes only profile identity fields into state.plan_reviewer_value (src/theforge/coordinator/plan_flow.py), unlike cost.agents ledgers.
  Suggestion: During implementation, either add resolved/configured identity capture to the plan-review value rows in plan_flow.py or document and implement a deterministic join in model_profiles_bridge.py against state.plan_review_results so plan-review value samples can be attributed to concrete served versions.

finding_registry.description: When preflight, planner, or review telemetry records both phase-level data and attempt-level data for the same invocation, the routing signal's resolved_population reports more attributed version runs than the signal's actual population contains.
When an alias resolves to version A, then version B, then version A again, alias_resolution_timeline reports current as version B even though the newest recorded invocation resolved to version A.

When a run record contains the final preflight invocation in both cost.agents and preflight.attempts, invocation_identity_rows emits two identity rows for the same preflight call, so alias-drift overstates the number of invocations for that configured model.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Keep aliases as valid routing candidates, add concrete-version candidates beside them, and make every recorded/evidence path carry both configured identity and resolved identity. The main implementation spine is: catalog expresses both names, canonicalization stops collapsing concrete versions into aliases, audit indexing exposes configured/resolved pairs per invocation, and profile consumers surface version composition instead of treating alias history as homogeneous.

steps.description: Add concrete-version catalog entries without removing family aliases
steps.details: Add pinned Anthropic CLI entries for the concrete versions already observed/priced in the codebase, alongside the existing sonnet/opus/haiku aliases. Keep alias-only configs valid. Extend legacy lookup aliases only where needed for raw provider spellings, and add tests proving alias and pinned entries coexist as separate registry ids and can both be selected through models.enabled/models.custom.

steps.description: Stop canonicalizing concrete served versions back to family aliases
steps.details: Change canonical_id_for_legacy_key so an observed concrete model such as claude-sonnet-4-6 resolves to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6/cli when that concrete entry exists, and otherwise remains visibly unresolved rather than being folded into anthropic/sonnet/cli. Update ledger divergence tests so configured alias and resolved concrete version are separate canonical identities with configured_differs_from_resolved true.

steps.description: Index configured and resolved identities for every recorded invocation
steps.details: Bump SUBSTRATE_SCHEMA_VERSION and add a role-neutral invocation identity index populated from existing per-entry ledgers under cost.agents, while keeping the current dev_* columns as compatibility projections. Store run_id, role/profile, configured identity/resolution, resolved identity/resolution, ledger_full, ledger_version, and differs. Rebuild/migration must derive this table from raw_json so old indexed runs gain the new query surface when their JSON carries ledgers.

steps.description: Attribute profile evidence to both the selected alias and the served version
steps.details: Extend RunOutcome/RoleAttempt/ReviewerAttempt data to carry configured and resolved identity separately where AgentResult already provides it. Fold alias-configured runs into the configured candidate's normal role bucket plus a by_resolved_model breakdown, and also fold the same admissible evidence under the concrete resolved model's own profile entry so pinned candidates can be ranked from prior alias-served runs. Ensure matching/read helpers do not merge alias and version identities accidentally.

steps.description: Expose version population in routing evidence and audit explainability
steps.details: Have get_dev_signal, get_dev_domain_signal, get_role_reliability_signal, get_review_signal, and reviewer value signals include the resolved-version population consulted for alias candidates, including count per resolved model and whether the population is mixed. Preserve existing rate/sample-floor behavior, but make routing_decision profile signals show when an alias's evidence spans multiple concrete versions.

steps.description: Make alias-resolution changes queryable from recorded runs
steps.details: Add a small read path over the invocation identity index that groups rows by configured alias and reports the ordered set of resolved identities over time. Surface it through the existing audits CLI area rather than inventing a separate storage file. Tests should prove two runs with the same configured alias and different resolved versions produce a detectable transition.

steps.description: Update documentation and contract tests for the new identity contract
steps.details: Document that model strings may be provider aliases or concrete versions, that aliases remain valid defaults, and that recorded runs distinguish configured identity from resolved served identity. Replace tests asserting alias/concrete equivalence with tests asserting separate identities plus explicit attribution.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A specific model version is expressible as a routing candidate for any provider that publishes versions, alongside — not instead of — the family alias.
Where a candidate names a family rather than a version, the version that served is recorded against the run and is distinguishable from the family name that selected it.
Evidence accumulated for a family alias is attributable to the versions that produced it, so a consumer can tell whether a population describes one model or several.
A change in what an alias resolves to is detectable from recorded runs rather than only from a behavioural surprise.
Nothing requires an operator to pin a version: a configuration naming only aliases keeps working and keeps tracking current releases.

risks.description: Existing migration logic intentionally collapsed Anthropic concrete versions into aliases, and tests currently encode that older contract.
risks.mitigation: Treat this as a deliberate contract change: update canonicalization, substrate migration, profile migration, and tests together so old behavior is not preserved accidentally.

risks.description: Folding evidence under both configured alias and resolved version can double count if readers match by provider/family instead of exact canonical identity.
risks.mitigation: Keep alias and version canonical ids distinct, make by_resolved_model a nested alias breakdown, and add reader tests proving alias queries and pinned-version queries return the intended populations only.

risks.description: The concrete Anthropic version list may drift as the provider advances aliases.
risks.mitigation: Seed only concrete versions already represented by observed runner/pricing data in the repo, and leave project-declared models.custom as the operator path for adding newly published versions without a code change.

risks.description: Role coverage is broader than the existing dev_* substrate columns.
risks.mitigation: Add a role-neutral invocation identity index instead of cloning dev columns per phase, while keeping dev_* as compatibility projections for current consumers.
